title: Persona-driven modular onboarding playbooks for first-run Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: New users (engineers, ML engineers, and platform admins) land in Console with varying goals and skill levels. Current first-run guidance is monolithic and assumes a single path, which leads to confusion on cost controls, rollouts, and model pinning.

Goal: Create a modular set of persona-driven "playbooks" — short, composable onboarding flows that appear in empty states and contextual help panels. Each playbook should steer users through 2–4 concrete tasks (e.g., set up a sandbox project, create a cost-aware endpoint, run a canary rollout) with inline templates, short demos, and pre-seeded snippets. Playbooks must be reusable across dashboards, rollouts, and cost views and be configurable by PM/Eng without a product release.

Scope: Design 3 core persona playbooks (Quick-Start Developer, Cost-Conscious Product Manager, Platform Admin - Compliance) + 2 micro-templates for rollouts and cost dashboards. Deliver high-fidelity Figma prototype, interaction spec, and acceptance criteria. Run unmoderated prototype tests (n≈18) and incorporate feedback into dev-ready handoff.

Non-goals: Deep changes to signup or account-level billing flows, multi-tenant RBAC redesign (handled by ENG-5123).
acceptance_criteria: Three persona playbooks designed and prototyped in Figma with full motion flows.
Playbooks can be invoked from empty states, the main dashboard, cost view, and rollout modal (specs include trigger rules).
Templates include copy, sample prompts/snippets, and a 'try in sandbox' button that points to seeded project creation flow.
Prototype usability score: >75% task success across 3 primary tasks in unmoderated test (create endpoint, pin model, run canary).
Design tokens and accessible color contrast pass WCAG AA for all UI elements in playbooks.
Implementation checklist and API contract for telemetry events delivered to ENG with clear event names and properties.
PM sign-off and a handoff package (Figma, interactions.md, acceptance checklist) uploaded to Confluence link below.
decisions: Make playbooks modular components (card + stepper + CTA) so they can be embedded in multiple empty states and the rollout modal.
Use a 'persona selector' progressive reveal rather than forced selection on first run to avoid blocking users who already know tasks.
Telemetry events will be namespaced as console.playbook.* and include persona, step, outcome, and user_tenure_days.
Initial rollout will be opt-in for existing customers; new signups will see a subtle banner linking to playbooks during first 7 days.
Cost templates will include an inline estimator that uses recent token consumption and perf profile to give a 7-day cost delta estimate.

user_testing_summary: Unmoderated prototype (n=18) across three personas. Key findings: (1) Developers completed 'create sandbox endpoint' in 82% of attempts, citing clear code snippets as the primary enabler. (2) PM persona misunderstood 'pin model' terminology; renamed to 'lock model version' improved clarity. (3) Cost estimator increased willingness to try canary from 47% to 63%. Action: adjust copy for model pinning and add an inline 'why this matters' tooltip for cost estimator.
